name: Cytarabine
route_note: continuous IV infusion (e.g. 7+3), high-dose IV, SC low dose, or intrathecal
originator: University of California, Berkeley; developed by Upjohn
owner: generic (many); Vyxeos held by Jazz Pharmaceuticals

discovery.by: Richard Walwick, Walden Roberts and Charles Dekker, UC Berkeley
discovery.note: Synthesised after Werner Bergmann discovered arabinose nucleosides in the Caribbean sponge Tectitethya crypta.

tagline: Sponge-inspired nucleoside that anchors induction therapy for acute myeloid leukaemia
summary: Cytarabine is a cytidine analogue with an arabinose sugar that is incorporated into DNA and blocks DNA polymerase, killing cells in S phase. It is the backbone of induction and consolidation therapy for acute myeloid leukaemia and is used in acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, lymphomas and CNS leukaemia.
mechanism: Cytarabine is taken up by nucleoside transporters and phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase to ara-CTP.

Ara-CTP competes with dCTP and is incorporated into DNA, where the arabinose 2′-hydroxyl hinders chain elongation and inhibits DNA polymerases, leading to replication fork stalling and apoptosis. Its action is strongly S-phase specific, which is why prolonged infusion or high doses are used.
uses: Acute myeloid leukaemia (induction with an anthracycline, high-dose consolidation)
Liposomal daunorubicin–cytarabine (Vyxeos) for therapy-related or MDS-related AML

history.title: Sponge nucleosides
history.detail: Bergmann and Feeney report spongothymidine and spongouridine from Tectitethya crypta.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Cytarabine is synthesised at UC Berkeley.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Cytosar (Upjohn) for acute leukaemia.

history.title: 7+3 regimen
history.detail: Yates and colleagues describe seven days of cytarabine with three days of daunorubicin, still the standard AML induction.

history.title: High-dose consolidation
history.detail: CALGB shows high-dose cytarabine consolidation improves outcomes in younger AML patients.

history.title: Vyxeos
history.detail: FDA approves liposomal daunorubicin and cytarabine (CPX-351) for therapy-related AML and AML with myelodysplasia-related changes.

pk.metabolism: cytidine deaminase deamination to ara-U (inactive), mainly in liver

serious: conjunctivitis (high dose; prevented with steroid eye drops)
safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning: should be given only by physicians experienced in cancer chemotherapy; potent bone-marrow suppressant.

facts: Marine sponge nucleosides inspired both cytarabine and the antiviral vidarabine.
